WHAT CHANGED. glsl/geom.c's emit_line() now generates silicon's footprint
instead of asking Vulkan for a line width, on the Vulkan path only. The
footprint is the intersection of the minor-axis band E = w(max + min/2)/max
with the slab between the two perpendicular butt caps; two bands intersect in a
parallelogram, so four vertices are exact. Choice 1 of the rule -- vertices
truncate to 1/16 px -- was already implemented in roundScreenCoords() in vsh.c
and is inherited by reading vtxPos. vk/draw.c forces the polygon mode to FILL
and culling off for those draws, and deletes the native line width path
entirely: every draw that puts a line on screen goes through
pgraph_glsl_need_geom(), so no line primitive reaches the rasteriser any more.
The GL renderer is untouched and keeps glLineWidth.

are VOID and the reading to compare is the 4-bit row of the table.

L2 -- WHY IT IS *NOT* 100.0000%, AND THIS IS SAID BEFORE THE ARM RUNS.

The bound file's E1 demands 100.0000%. I PREDICT E1 WILL NOT BE MET, and that

The emitted parallelogram's corners are quantised by the rasteriser to
1/2^subPixelPrecisionBits of a device pixel. Because the line endpoints are
already on a 1/16 grid and the same offset vector is added at both ends, that
quantisation TRANSLATES both long edges by one constant vector rather than
shearing them -- so the band moves bodily by up to one quantum. Of the goldens'
41,892 band edges, 1,911 (4.562%) land EXACTLY on a pixel centre and need the
low-open tie-break, and a further 143 sit within 1/256 of one without being on
it. Those 143 are the cuts that can go either way.

A sharp optimum at exactly one quantum: below it the rasteriser's own vertex

registered near-miss band -- i.e. it would have read as "widened correctly,
phase wrong" when the phase was right.
